last_attempts_log.asr_text: When I leave a notice saying nobody was home and head off, I feel a little down, too. But then I go to the next house. I really would like to see fewer redeliveries, and they are hard on us, too. Even so, I can't just say that customers should pay the cost. I think it makes more sense to cover the cost through the overall fee for carrying packages than to charge each customer who wasn't home for the cost of that redelivery. To do that, I want the company to think about whether free shipping for online orders should stay as it is. If they review shipping fees, I want them to review how the fees are set, too, so that the money really reaches the people who deliver the packages.

last_attempts_log.asr_text: Having to pay for re-delivery just doesn't sit right with me. My husband and I are both away at work, so for packages where we can choose a delivery time, we choose a day and time when we know we'll be home. But once, I chose a morning time slot and the package didn't come. I went out to take care of an errand, and when I got back, there was a missed delivery notice. There are also many packages where you can't choose a time, and you don't know beforehand when they'll arrive. Before charging us, I want them to first do something about arriving at the time we chose and telling us when the package will arrive. The delivery workers must have a hard time because there aren't enough of them, and I guess it can't be helped, but I can't accept having to pay for that. Am I wrong to feel this way?

last_attempts_log.asr_text: I try to pick up packages at a delivery office or locker so I don’t cause trouble with redelivery. It’s convenient to pick them up when it suits me, but for some items, I can’t choose a locker. And even when I ask for a package to be sent to a delivery office, it may arrive late, so I sometimes end up receiving it in person after all. Still, I take the trouble to think about how to receive my packages, so honestly, I think it’s wrong that I pay the same fee as people who are always away and ask for redelivery. Redelivery takes up the delivery worker’s time, so it’s fine to charge for it. I’d be happy if the first redelivery were free and people who are repeatedly away had to pay. But maybe that’s just my point of view, since the delivery office is nearby and I can choose how to receive my packages.
